chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad all together, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kanani, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For the sun there are three hundred and sixty constellations (buruj). Each of them is like an island from the islands of Arabia. So it descends each day upon one of these constellations. So when it sets, it reaches the limit of the underside of the Throne. It does not cease prostrating until the next day. Then it is returned to the place of its rising, and with it are two angels who hail with it. And indeed, its face is towards the people of the sky and its back is towards the people of the earth. And if its face were towards the people of the earth, the earth and those upon it would be burnt due to the intensity of its heat.'

And the meaning of its prostration is what He, Glorified and Exalted, said: 'Do you not see that to Allah bow down in worship all things that are in the heavens and on earth, the sun, the moon, the stars; the hills, the trees, the animals; and a great number among mankind?'

key_terms.بُرْجاً: Constellation or mansion (one of the 360 divisions of the ecliptic)

ai.seo_question: What is the cosmological description of the sun's movement and prostration in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in *Al-Kafi* presents a detailed cosmological model where the sun traverses 360 'constellations' (buruj), each likened to an Arabian island, prostrating beneath the Throne until its return. The narration clarifies that the sun's orientation—face to the heavens and back to the earth—prevents terrestrial incineration, linking this physical motion to the Quranic concept of universal prostration (sujud) by celestial and terrestrial entities. This interpretation aligns with Shia exegetical traditions that view natural phenomena as active participants in divine worship.

en.hubeali: H 14596 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin ziyad altogether, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kanany, from Al-Asbagh Bin Nabata who said:

Amir-ul-Momineenasws said: ‘For the sun there are three hundred constellations. Each of the constellations from these is like an island from the islands of Arabia. So it descends upon a constellation from these each day. So when it disappears, it ends up to the limits beneath the Throne. It does not stop prostrating until the next day. Then it returns to the place of its rising, and with it are two Angels who hail with it and turn its face towards the people of the sky reversing it from the people of the earth. And had it faced the people of the earth, it would have burnt down the earth and the ones upon it due to the intensity of its heat.

And the meaning of its prostration is what the Glorious and the High has Said: “[22:18] Do you not see that to Allah bow down in worship all things that are in the heavens and on earth, the sun, the moon, the stars; the hills, the trees, the animals; and a great number among mankind?”
